title: Basic probability · a small concept graph
subtitle: Click any node for everything the notes say about it. Its neighbours stay lit.

start.heading: The spine
items: Everything is built by counting weight over subsets of outcomes.

legend.interp: what a result means in plain terms

tagNote: Tags such as “N1·N2” show every note that repeats a concept; the graph keeps it once.

OM.label:
Sample space
Ω = all outcomes
details: The set of everything that could happen in one run of an experiment.
Outcomes are mutually exclusive and together exhaustive.

EV.label:
Event
A ⊆ Ω
details: A subset of outcomes: the thing whose probability we want.
Set operations on events mean or, and, not.

PR.label:
Probability axioms
P(A) ≥ 0, P(Ω) = 1
details: Probabilities are non-negative and total one.

CP.label:
Conditional probability
P(A|B) = P(A∩B) / P(B)
details: Restrict the sample space to B, then renormalize.
CP.example: P(even | roll > 3) = 2/3, since {4, 6} are the even outcomes among {4, 5, 6}.

IND.label:
Independence
P(A∩B) = P(A)P(B)
details: Learning B leaves the probability of A unchanged.

TOT.label:
Law of total probability
P(A) = Σ P(A|Bi) P(Bi)
details: Split A across a partition of Ω and add the pieces.

BAYES.label:
Bayes' rule
P(B|A) = P(A|B) P(B) / P(A)
details: Follows from writing P(A∩B) two ways.
The denominator usually comes from the law of total probability.
BAYES.example: A 99% accurate test for a 1-in-1000 condition: P(condition | positive) ≈ 9%.

INTERP.label: Prior → posterior
details: Bayes' rule updates a belief P(B) into P(B|A) after seeing evidence A.

FALLACY.label: P(A|B) is not P(B|A)
details: Swapping the two ignores the base rate, as the test example shows.
